title: Customer Onboarding and KYC Policy
body:
Purpose: verify every borrower, guarantor and beneficial owner before funds are released.

Scope: all regulated and unregulated loans, direct and introduced.

Process:
1. Application captured in the origination platform (direct web form or introducer portal).
2. Identity and address verified electronically through the KYC vendor; Companies House and PSC register checked for limited companies.
3. Sanctions and PEP screening run by the third-party screening vendor at onboarding and nightly thereafter.
4. Customer risk rating (low / medium / high) assigned by rules; high risk routed to Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) by the Financial Crime team.
5. Source of funds evidenced for loans above £250,000.

Controls:
- C-ONB-01 No drawdown until KYC status = Passed.
- C-ONB-02 EDD sign-off by MLRO delegate for high-risk customers.
- C-ONB-03 Introducer-supplied documents are re-verified independently; Northbridge does not rely on an introducer's own checks.
- C-ONB-04 Screening vendor match rules reviewed annually by the MLRO.

title: Anti-Money Laundering, Counter-Terrorist Financing and Sanctions Policy
body:
Purpose: meet the Money Laundering Regulations 2017, SYSC 6.3 and the UK financial sanctions regime, and follow the FCA Financial Crime Guide.

Key elements:
- Firm-wide business risk assessment refreshed annually, mapped to the FCA Financial Crime Guide chapters.
- Customer due diligence per POL-ONB; ongoing monitoring of repayments for unusual overpayments, third-party payments and early settlement from unexplained sources.
- Suspicious activity reporting to the NCA via the MLRO; tipping-off training for all staff.
- Sanctions: real-time screening via the third-party vendor; asset freeze procedures; reporting to OFSI.
- Proliferation financing is not separately assessed today (considered low risk for a domestic SME lender).

Controls:
- C-AML-01 Annual business-wide risk assessment approved by the Board.
- C-AML-02 Transaction monitoring rules reviewed every 12 months.
- C-AML-03 MLRO annual report to the Board.
- C-AML-04 Independent AML audit every two years (last: 2025).

title: Fraud Prevention Policy
body:
Purpose: prevent first-party, third-party and introducer fraud in lending.

Controls:
- C-FRD-01 Bank statement and accounting data pulled directly via open banking / accounting integrations; uploaded PDFs flagged for document-tamper checks.
- C-FRD-02 Device and email risk scoring at application.
- C-FRD-03 Introducer fraud: monthly analysis of approval, default and early-arrears rates by introducer; outliers trigger review under POL-INTRO.
- C-FRD-04 Payee confirmation (Confirmation of Payee) before drawdown.
- C-FRD-05 Fraud typologies library updated quarterly, including AI-generated documents and synthetic identities.

The policy references the FCA Financial Crime Guide fraud chapter as its external standard.

title: Introducer and Broker Oversight Policy
body:
Purpose: govern the ~60 introducers who refer applications, including commercial finance brokers (FCA-authorised for credit broking where regulated loans are introduced) and asset-finance and invoice-finance firms that are not FCA-authorised.

Onboarding of an introducer:
1. Introducer agreement signed.
2. FCA Register check for authorised brokers.
3. For non-authorised firms: Companies House check and a self-declaration questionnaire covering ownership, financial crime controls and complaints.
4. Risk tier assigned (A/B/C).

Ongoing:
- Annual attestation by each introducer.
- Quarterly MI on volumes, conversion and arrears (see C-FRD-03).

Gap noted in 2025 internal audit (open): MLR registration status of non-authorised introducers is taken from the introducer's self-declaration and is not independently verified.

Controls:
- C-INT-01 No referrals accepted before onboarding is complete.
- C-INT-02 Annual attestation.
- C-INT-03 Tier C introducers reviewed every 6 months.

title: Credit Risk and Affordability Policy
body:
Purpose: lend responsibly and within risk appetite; meet CONC 5 creditworthiness rules for regulated loans.

Decisioning:
- Applications up to £50,000 are decided automatically by the rules engine using the credit bureau scorecard, open-banking affordability metrics and policy rules. Declines are fully automated; referrals go to an underwriter.
- Above £50,000: underwriter decision with automated pre-assessment.
- Customers declined automatically are told the main reasons and may request human review (supports UK GDPR Article 22 rights).

Controls:
- C-CRD-01 Scorecard performance monitored monthly (Gini, PSI) by the Credit Risk team.
- C-CRD-02 Override rates reported to Credit Committee.
- C-CRD-03 Vendor scorecard changes assessed before go-live under POL-AI.
- C-CRD-04 Human review of any automated decline on request within 5 working days.

title: AI and Model Risk Governance Policy
body:
Purpose: govern every model and AI system used in decisions about customers.

Model inventory (current):
- M1 Credit bureau scorecard (vendor-supplied, black-box score with reason codes).
- M2 Affordability rules engine (in-house).
- M3 Transaction monitoring rules (in-house).
- M4 'Nudge' collections assistant pilot: an LLM-based agent that sends arrears messages, answers customer questions and proposes payment plans within limits set by Collections. Pilot covers 400 customers in 1–30 days arrears.

Requirements:
- Each model has an owner, a risk tier, documentation and a validation schedule.
- Vendor models: Northbridge relies on vendor validation reports; independent validation of vendor models is not currently performed.
- Generative / agentic AI: human-in-the-loop required for any payment plan above £200/month or longer than 12 months; prompts and outputs logged for 2 years.
- A Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) is required before any model processing personal data goes live.

Controls:
- C-AI-01 Annual model inventory attestation.
- C-AI-02 Drift monitoring for M1 and M2 monthly; M4 weekly sample QA of 50 conversations.
- C-AI-03 Change control: any prompt or tool change to M4 approved by Head of Collections and CRO.

title: Collections and Recoveries Process
body:
Purpose: support customers in financial difficulty and recover debt fairly, in line with CONC 7 and the Consumer Duty.

Process:
1. Day 1–5 missed payment: automated reminder (SMS/email). In the Nudge pilot, the agent sends the reminder and can open a conversation.
2. Day 6–30: Nudge or a collections agent explores the customer's situation, signposts free debt advice (MoneyHelper, StepChange, Business Debtline) and offers forbearance options: reduced payments, payment holiday, term extension.
3. Vulnerability indicators detected (by staff or by Nudge keyword and sentiment flags) are routed to the Specialist Support team per POL-VULN.
4. Day 31–90: arrears letters and Notice of Sums in Arrears (regulated loans).
5. Day 90+: default and recoveries; third-party debt collection agency for unregulated loans only.

Controls:
- C-COL-01 No more than 3 contact attempts per week.
- C-COL-02 Forbearance outcomes QA-sampled monthly (20 cases).
- C-COL-03 Nudge conversation transcripts retained and reviewed weekly (see C-AI-02).
- C-COL-04 Customers can ask to speak to a person at any point in a Nudge conversation.

title: Vulnerable Customers Policy
body:
Purpose: identify and support customers with characteristics of vulnerability (health, life events, resilience, capability), following FCA FG21/1 and the Consumer Duty.

Applies to sole traders and partners with regulated loans, and to the individuals behind small limited companies where they are personally guaranteeing a loan.

Key elements:
- Staff trained annually to recognise vulnerability; flags recorded with customer consent.
- Specialist Support team handles flagged cases; collections activity paused for up to 30 days on a vulnerability flag.
- Automated channels (including the Nudge pilot) must escalate on vulnerability indicators and must not make the final decision on forbearance for a flagged customer.

Controls:
- C-VUL-01 Vulnerability MI reported quarterly to the Board's Consumer Duty champion.
- C-VUL-02 Outcomes of flagged vs non-flagged customers compared twice a year.

title: Consumer Duty Framework
body:
Purpose: deliver good outcomes for retail customers (regulated borrowers) across the four outcomes: products and services, price and value, consumer understanding, consumer support.

Key elements:
- Annual Board report on customer outcomes (last approved July 2026).
- Outcome testing: communications testing, fair value assessment, support journey testing (including digital and AI-assisted journeys).
- Board Consumer Duty champion: Non-Executive Director.

Controls:
- C-CD-01 Annual Board report.
- C-CD-02 New or changed customer journeys (including AI-assisted ones) require a Consumer Duty impact assessment before launch.

title: Complaints Handling Policy
body:
Purpose: handle complaints in line with DISP 1, including final responses within 8 weeks and Financial Ombudsman referral rights for eligible complainants (micro-enterprises and sole traders).

Controls:
- C-CMP-01 Root cause analysis quarterly.
- C-CMP-02 Complaints about automated decisions or the Nudge assistant tagged separately for MI.
- C-CMP-03 Complaint data reported to the FCA twice a year.

title: Data Protection and Privacy Policy
body:
Purpose: comply with UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018 and the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025.

Key elements:
- Record of processing activities maintained by the DPO.
- DPIAs required for high-risk processing, including automated credit decisions (POL-CREDIT) and the Nudge collections assistant (DPIA approved March 2026 for the pilot only).
- Automated decision-making: customers informed in the privacy notice; right to human review honoured (C-CRD-04).
- Transparency: privacy notice explains use of AI in collections communications.
- Data subject rights requests answered within one month.

Controls:
- C-DAT-01 DPIA register reviewed quarterly.
- C-DAT-02 Privacy notice reviewed annually or when processing changes.
- C-DAT-03 Regulatory horizon scanning for ICO guidance owned by the DPO.

title: Information Security Policy
body:
Purpose: protect customer data and systems.

Key elements:
- ISO 27001-aligned controls; annual penetration test.
- Access reviews quarterly; MFA for all staff.
- Data loss prevention on email and endpoints.
- Third-party AI services may only receive customer data under a signed data processing agreement and with data residency in the UK or EEA.

Controls:
- C-SEC-01 Annual penetration test.
- C-SEC-02 Quarterly access review.
- C-SEC-03 Security incident reporting to DPO within 24 hours.

title: Third-Party and Outsourcing Risk Policy
body:
Purpose: manage risks from suppliers, outsourcers and partners, including SYSC 8 material outsourcing.

Critical third parties: KYC vendor, sanctions screening vendor, credit bureau, cloud hosting provider, LLM API provider used by the Nudge pilot.

Key elements:
- Due diligence at onboarding; annual review for critical suppliers.
- Exit plans for material outsourcing.
- Performance and incident MI monthly.

Controls:
- C-TPR-01 Annual review of critical suppliers.
- C-TPR-02 Exit plan tested every two years.
- C-TPR-03 Financial crime controls supplied by third parties (screening, KYC) are tested by Northbridge at least annually rather than relying on vendor assurance alone.

title: Governance, SM&CR and Conduct Rules Policy
body:
Purpose: maintain clear accountability under the Senior Managers and Certification Regime (core firm).

Key elements:
- Senior Managers: SMF1 CEO, SMF3 Executive Director, SMF9 Chair, SMF16 Compliance Oversight, SMF17 MLRO, SMF29 Limited Scope.
- Statements of Responsibilities kept current and resubmitted to the FCA on material change; Management Responsibilities Map maintained by the Company Secretary (enhanced-firm style, voluntarily).
- Certification Regime: 38 certified staff (underwriters, collections team leaders, introducer managers); annual fitness and propriety assessment each October; certificates issued by HR.
- Conduct Rules training annually for all staff; breaches reported to the FCA.

Controls:
- C-GOV-01 Annual certification cycle (October).
- C-GOV-02 Statements of Responsibilities reviewed every 6 months.
- C-GOV-03 Conduct Rules training completion above 98%.

title: Financial Promotions and Marketing Policy
body:
Purpose: ensure promotions for regulated credit are clear, fair and not misleading (CONC 3) and support consumer understanding under the Consumer Duty.

Controls:
- C-FPR-01 Compliance sign-off for every promotion before release.
- C-FPR-02 Introducer marketing materials that name Northbridge are approved by Northbridge.
- C-FPR-03 Representative APR shown wherever required.
